subject: SOC 2: CI/CD deploy gate, rollforward plan & secrets custody
messages:
From: KPMG Audit Team <audit@kpmg.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@finbank.com>
Date: 2027-12-05T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: SOC 2 evidence request: CI/CD deploy gate, rollforward and secrets proof

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking this — FinBank's SOC 2 engagement team is collecting technical artefacts related to your SDLC and deploy controls. For scope, please provide the following for our SOC 2 trust-services testing:

1) Deploy gate / acceptance criteria: a short description of the CI/CD gating conditions (PR checks, tests, approvals, OPA/rego policies) and screenshots or logs showing an example successful/blocked deployment.
2) Rollforward / rollback playbook: the runbook for emergency rollforward and rollback (including who can trigger, required approvals, and typical RTO), and one example incident in the last 12 months where the plan was executed.
3) Code review enforcement: evidence that code-review and merge gates cannot be bypassed (policy page or tooling config, e.g., branch protection rules).
4) Secrets management & rotation: owner mapping for secrets, rotation schedule, and proof of a rotation cycle (artifact: rotation ledger or rotation job logs).
5) Audit logs: CI/CD audit logs for deploy-related actions for the last 90 days (include deploy id, user, timestamp, target environment, and action).
6) Ephemeral credentials: short description of the ephemeral token/certificate workflow used for runners/agents and whether rotation is automated via KMS/HSM.

If you can provide the items above as attachments or links by EOD Tuesday (2027-12-07) that would keep us on schedule. If anything needs a quick screen-share to walk through, let us know and we can book time.

Thanks,
KPMG Audit Team
KPMG - Cloud & Technology Assurance

- Audit logs (90 days): attaching audit-log-extract-202709-202712.csv (sanitized, deploy events only). Karthik will confirm the log export format below.

ETA: initial package attached to this thread. If you need raw, non-sanitized logs or a live session to verify metadata, we can schedule a 30-minute call on Wednesday 12/08.

Best,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-12-06T08:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence request: CI/CD deploy gate, rollforward and secrets proof

Priya — confirming the exports and providing the technical context for the auditor: 

1) CI/CD deploy gate: We enforce PR-required checks in GitHub with branch protection (status checks + 2 approvers). The OPA policy (ci-policy-opa.rego) runs as a step in our pipeline; any policy failure fails the job. Example blocked run log (sanitized):

-- LOG SNIPPET --
2027-11-22T14:12:03Z, deploy-job-9821, user: alice@redwoodinference.com, status: blocked, reason: policy/forbidden-docker-image
-- END --

2) Rollforward/rollback: deploy-runbook.pdf contains the runbook and a recent example (incident ID RD-20270618) where we performed a controlled rollback to the prior release within 18 minutes; runbook assigns roles: SRE level-2 can trigger, product/eng lead must be notified.

3) Audit logs: audit-log-extract-202709-202712.csv contains fields: deploy_id,timestamp,user,action,target_env,commit_sha. We redacted internal IPs and expanded user display to email.

4) Secrets rotation: secrets-rotation-ledger.csv lists secret_id,owner,rotation_schedule,next_rotation,rotation_job_id. We rotate critical credentials every 30 days via an automated job backed by customer-managed KMS. Owner mapping is in the ledger.

5) Ephemeral credentials: ephemeral-token-workflow.md describes how our CI runners request time-limited tokens from a token broker service which in turn uses KMS to sign short-lived credentials. Tokens default to 1-hour TTL; tasks that require longer lifetimes must request explicit approval and are audited.

If the auditors want a sample Terraform/CI snippet showing token request or the KMS signing policy, I can paste an obfuscated snippet here or attach a small example file.

Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifying questions after review of the artifacts: 

- Ephemeral tokens TTL: you mention 1-hour TTL by default. Can you confirm whether these tokens are issued per CI job run and whether the token broker enforces single-use or re-use across steps? Auditors typically look for single-use or strong mitigation when reuse is allowed.

- KMS usage: is the KMS customer-managed with a defined key-access policy (please confirm key rotation / key-ownership mapping)?

- Rotation evidence: can you provide one example rotation job log (timestamp + rotation_job_id from the ledger) showing the rotation completed end-to-end (we just need a sanitized snippet).

If you can drop the answers and the single rotation job log snippet into this thread, that should be sufficient. Otherwise we can schedule a quick call.

Best,
KPMG Audit Team

Hi — quick answers and an attached rotation log snippet.

- Token TTL and usage: Tokens are issued per CI job run by default and scoped to the job's pipeline id; reuse across unrelated pipeline runs is not allowed. Steps within the same pipeline can reuse the token for the duration of the job (this is required for multi-step builds). The token broker enforces job-scoped issuance and keeps an audit trail with job_id, issued_at, and requester identity. Default TTL is 1 hour; tokens are revocable by SRE operators.

- KMS: yes — we use a customer-managed key (CMK) in our cloud KMS for signing. Key ownership and ACLs are defined in our key-access policy (see deploy-runbook.pdf appendix B). Key rotation for the CMK is on an 18-month schedule; rotation operations are logged and require two-person approval.

- Rotation job proof: Attached is a sanitized snippet from rotation_job_id ROT-20271112-77 showing start, key-id referenced, rotation steps, and completion status.

If the auditors want the raw rotation job logs, we can provide them under an NDA; otherwise the snippet should be sufficient. I'm also available for a 30-minute walkthrough Wednesday 12/08 at 10:30am PST if you'd like to go through anything live.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
